body:
Relay BB run pushed an update.

Pull request: #345

Tokens: 0 · Cost: $0.0000

Pushed branch `bb/relay-139-auth-v1-01-08-create-the-authenticatio-thr_ygancw5etr` to origin.

## Summary

Implements issue #139: creates the auth-v1 database schema and token primitives.

- **Migration** `0016_auth_schema.sql`: extends `users` with `email` (unique), `password_hash`, and `locale` (default `cs`); adds `sessions` (multi-session per user, unique `token_hash`, `platform` restricted to `web`/`ios`/`macos`, expiry/revocation lookup index) and `login_attempts` (email+IP+recency index for throttling).
- **Primitives** in `backend/packages/data/src/auth/`: Argon2id password hashing (`@node-rs/argon2`), opaque session-token generation/hashing (SHA-256), and constant-time comparison — no JWTs.
- **Repositories**: `usersStore`, `sessionsStore`, `loginAttemptsStore`, all exported from the package index.
- **Tests**: unit tests for the crypto primitives and an integration suite covering duplicate email/token rejection, multiple live sessions per user, active-session filtering (expired/revoked), and login-attempt throttling counts.

Verified: full `pnpm run test` (unit, integration, e2e), workspace-wide `tsc -b`, and `check:boundaries` all clean, aside from one pre-existing, unrelated, timing-sensitive flaky test in `propertyTypeMigration.test.ts`.

Branch: `bb/relay-139-auth-v1-01-08-create-the-authenticatio-thr_ygancw5etr`

This branch implements issue #139 (auth-v1 01/08): extends `users` with `email`/`password_hash`/`locale`, adds `sessions` and `login_attempts` tables, and adds token primitives (Argon2id password hashing via `@node-rs/argon2`, opaque session tokens hashed with SHA-256 for storage, constant-time comparison). It has since been merged with `develop` to resolve a conflict (including a migration-ordinal collision, resolved by renumbering to `0025_auth_schema.sql`) and a knock-on test regression in unrelated approval-request tests that inserted bare `users` rows. Full test suite (unit/integration/e2e), migration numbering check, dependency-boundary check, and typecheck all pass cleanly.
